Compound (C): 1-(4-Fluorobenzyl)-3-methyl-2-oxo-spiro[indoline-3,4′-pyrrolidine]-1-carboxylate  
Molecular formula: C20H18FN2O3  

1. Precursors  
   • Isatin (1H-indole-2,3-dione)  
   • L-Proline  
   • Formaldehyde (37% aqueous)  
   • Sodium cyanoborohydride  
   • 4-Fluorobenzyl bromide  
   • Potassium carbonate  
   • Ethanol  
   • Concentrated H2SO4  
   • Dry DMF  
   • Standard organic solvents for work-up/purification  

2. Step-by-step synthesis  

Step 1: Spirooxindole core formation (Mannich-type cyclization)  
   • Combine isatin (0.01 mol) and L-proline (0.012 mol) in ethanol (50 mL).  
   • Add catalytic HCl (0.1 mL), reflux 6 h.  
   • Cool, filter off pale-yellow spirooxindole (I).  
   Yield ~80%.  

Step 2: Reductive N-methylation  
   • Dissolve (I) (0.008 mol) in MeOH (30 mL), cool to 0 °C.  
   • Add formaldehyde (0.016 mol) dropwise, stir 30 min.  
   • Add NaCNBH3 (0.012 mol) portionwise, 0 → RT over 2 h.  
   • Quench with sat. NH4Cl, extract with EtOAc.  
   • Dry, concentrate to give N-methyl-spirooxindole (II).  
   Yield ~75%.  

Step 3: N-Alkylation with 4-fluorobenzyl bromide  
   • To (II) (0.006 mol) in dry DMF (20 mL) add K2CO3 (0.01 mol) and 4-fluorobenzyl bromide (0.007 mol).  
   • Stir at 60 °C for 8 h under N2.  
   • Cool, dilute with H2O, extract EtOAc.  
   • Wash, dry, concentrate to N-benzyl derivative (III).  
   Yield ~65%.  

Step 4: Esterification to ethyl carboxylate  
   • Dissolve (III) (0.005 mol) in EtOH (25 mL), add H2SO4 (0.2 mL).  
   • Reflux 4 h.  
   • Cool, neutralize with NaHCO3, extract with CH2Cl2.  
   • Dry, concentrate to crude ester (IV).  
   Yield ~70%.  

Step 5: Purification  
   • Load (IV) onto silica gel (230–400 mesh).  
   • Elute with hexane/EtOAc gradient (8:2 → 5:5).  
   • Collect fractions containing pure C (monitored by TLC, Rf ~0.45 in 1:1 hexane/EtOAc).  
   • Evaporate solvent to yield white crystalline title compound.  
   Overall yield ~28% (five steps).  

3. Key reaction types & mechanistic notes  
   • Mannich-type cyclization: nucleophilic addition of proline amine to isatin C-3, intramolecular ring closure to spirooxindole.  
   • Reductive amination: iminium formation with formaldehyde, hydride delivery from NaCNBH3 selectively installs N-methyl.  
   • SN2 N-alkylation: deprotonated secondary amine attacks benzyl bromide.  
   • Fischer esterification: acid-catalyzed conversion of carboxylic acid to ethyl ester.  

4. Isolation & characterization  
   • Verify each intermediate by 1H NMR (imine vs. amine signals in I vs. II), 13C NMR (spiro carbon ~80 ppm), and ESI-MS.  
   • Final compound C: 1H NMR (400 MHz, CDCl3) δ 7.50–6.80 (m, ArH), 4.80 (s, spiro-CH), 3.50 (s, N-CH3), 3.30 (s, CH2Ph), 1.30 (t, J = 7.1 Hz, OCH2CH3); 13C NMR shows carbonyls at ~175 and ~162 ppm; MS m/z [M+H]+ = 349.  

5. Notes on reagent interactions  
   • L-Proline’s secondary amine and carboxylic acid both direct cyclization; pH control critical.  
   • NaCNBH3 selectively reduces iminium over isolated ketones.  
   • K2CO3 in DMF ensures complete deprotonation for SN2; excess base minimizes O-alkylation.  
   • Acid strength in esterification balances rate vs. side hydrolysis.  

This five-step route affords the target spiro-oxindole carboxylate in multi-tens-percent overall yield and illustrates condensation, reductive amination, SN2 and esterification in a concise, academic-style protocol.
